title: L5-F1: checkpoint/replay restore must preserve runtime-significant insertion chronology (combatant, combat instance, bind credit)
description:
Independent audit lane L5 (eshyra-o9bd.16.5 notes, full evidence and reproducers) found a BLOCKER. Checkpoint serialization (persistence/checkpoint/serialize.ts:84-89) sorts rows by canonical JSON. Both checkpoint materialization (checkpoint/store.ts:102-118) and replay restore (campaign/turnReplayStore.ts:109-125) re-INSERT named columns only, which assigns fresh implicit rowids.
Consumers that order by rowid then change behavior after restore while replayStateHash stays identical:
- encounterCombatants.ts:329, 1187 (current actor projection: i.rowid DESC, c.rowid DESC), 3208, 3337, 3449, 3524 (findLiveActorCombatantId), 3650;
- activeEffects.ts:8475 (combat closure skips older projections by rowid);
- itemGrantBinding.ts:431 (oldest open credit: ORDER BY issued_at, rowid).
Reproducer A: Find Familiar with nine dismiss/recall pairs. After restore, the latest-row choice moves from c-fam-10 to c-fam-9; update_combatant desyncs the durable actor's HP, and close_combat_instance writes the actor as absent at stale HP.
Reproducer B: ten Bowl of Commanding Water Elementals uses with equal issued_at. Credit order goes from 1..10 to 1,10,2..9.
Precedent: migration 0029_persistent_event_order.sql fixed the same class for scene_log and character_wallet_event with an explicit insertion_order column.
design:
Follow the 0029 precedent exactly.
1. Migration 0053_<name>.sql. Add insertion_order INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 to encounter_combatant, combat_instance and item_grant_bind_credit; backfill it from rowid; add a unique index per table, as in 0029.
2. Producers (encounterCombatants.ts:1911 and :2424, itemGrantBinding.ts:304, plus any other INSERT into these tables) allocate (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(insertion_order),0)+1 FROM <table>) inside the INSERT, as scene.ts:264 does.
3. Replace every rowid ordering or comparison on these tables with insertion_order. Grep all of packages/core/src for rowid.
4. characterChronicle.ts uses rowid as well. Verify whether its tables travel through campaign checkpoint/replay. If they do, fix them the same way. If they do not, document why in the guard allowlist.
5. Add a structural guard test: no SQL 'rowid' in packages/core/src outside an explicit, justified allowlist.
6. Permanent evidence: generalized round-trip behavioral invariants through BOTH checkpoint serialize/materialize AND in-place replay restore. Cover repeated admissions of one durable actor with 10+ rows whose IDs sort differently from chronology, and equal-timestamp credit issuance with 10+ credits. Assert the live actor identity, HP sync with the durable actor after update_combatant, presence and HP after close_combat_instance, and oldest-credit selection. Extend the existing checkpoint/encounterCombatants/itemGrantBindCredit suites.
Make sure pre-0053 checkpoints still restore: check how checkpoint schema versioning and migrations handle restored snapshots (see how 0029 handled checkpoint.schemaIntegrity). Update migration count/parity pins only where they are counts, with justification. Do not weaken any test.
acceptance_criteria: Both reproducers produce identical behavior before and after restore; all rowid consumers on checkpointed tables use durable order; guard test in place; verify:worktree passes; commit on branch.
notes:
Implementation commit: 9a2e954f8807d02990bbc663e36b066979194f63.

Verification: `npm run verify:worktree` passed. Vitest reported 388 files passed, 2 skipped; 7,256 tests passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed. The skipped cases are the suite's documented integration gates.

Rowid consumer dispositions:
- `state/encounterCombatants.ts`: the current active actor projection selector, `currentActorProjectionId`, `updateCampaignActor`, `revertCampaignActorToNaturalForm`, `removeCampaignActorFromPlay`, `restoreBondedCampaignActor`, `findLiveActorCombatantId`, and `recallPocketedCampaignActor` now use `insertion_order` on `encounter_combatant` and/or `combat_instance`.
- `state/activeEffects.ts` combat closure's newer-projection comparison now uses `encounter_combatant.insertion_order`.
- `state/itemGrantBinding.ts` oldest open credit ordering now uses `issued_at, insertion_order` on `item_grant_bind_credit`.
- `character/characterChronicle.ts` retains its record and event `rowid` tiebreaks. The chronicle tables live in the separate character-registry SQLite store, not the campaign database; checkpoint serialization and turn-replay snapshots cannot include them. This is documented as the sole SQL rowid allowlist entry in `test/rowidSqlGuard.test.ts`.
- `state/domainMutations.ts` uses the TypeScript local `rowId` for inventory identifiers, not SQLite `rowid`; no SQL rowid consumer remains there.
- Migration 0053 uses `rowid` only to backfill durable order for pre-migration rows, following migration 0029.

Pre-0053 checkpoints: their snapshots materialize with the captured version-52 schema and remain restorable. On normal campaign database open, `initSchema` runs the versioned migration runner and applies migration 0053, adding/backfilling the order columns and unique indexes. A checkpoint restore regression test builds and materializes an actual through-0052 schema to verify this upgrade path.

Migration count pins updated from 52 to 53; no rules-pack or freeze files changed.
